title: Khirokitia
description: Farmers build a walled village of round stone houses, one of the best preserved Neolithic sites of the eastern Mediterranean.

title: Evagoras takes Salamis
description: Evagoras seizes the throne of the largest city of the island and tries to unite Cyprus against Persia.

title: Rome annexes Cyprus
description: Rome takes the island from the Ptolemies and sends Cato the Younger to carry it out.

title: First Arab raid
description: A fleet under Muawiyah sacks the capital, and for three centuries the island lies between the empire and the caliphate.

title: Cyprus shared by treaty
description: Justinian II and the caliph Abd al-Malik agree to share the taxes of the island, which neither garrisons.

title: Byzantine reconquest
description: Under Nikephoros II Phokas the empire takes back full control of the island.

title: Richard the Lionheart takes Cyprus
description: On his way to the Third Crusade the English king overthrows the island's self-proclaimed emperor Isaac Komnenos, ending Byzantine rule.

title: Lusignan kingdom founded
description: Guy of Lusignan, who has lost the crown of Jerusalem, buys the island, and his family rules it as a crusader kingdom for three centuries.

title: Genoese take Famagusta
description: A Genoese fleet seizes the kingdom's main port and keeps it for ninety years.

title: Battle of Khirokitia
description: A Mamluk army captures King Janus, and the kingdom becomes a tributary of Egypt.

title: Venice takes over Cyprus
description: Queen Catherine Cornaro, a Venetian, is made to give up the kingdom to the republic.

title: Ottomans take Nicosia
description: An Ottoman army storms the capital after a siege of seven weeks.

title: Fall of Famagusta
description: The last Venetian fortress surrenders after almost a year, and the island becomes Ottoman for three centuries.

title: Execution of Archbishop Kyprianos
description: When Greece rises, the Ottoman governor hangs the archbishop and puts to death the bishops and leading Greek Cypriots.

title: Cyprus Convention
description: The sultan lets Britain occupy and administer the island in return for support against Russia.

title: Britain annexes Cyprus
description: When the Ottoman Empire enters the war, Britain annexes the island it has administered since 1878.

title: October revolt
description: Greek Cypriots demanding union with Greece burn down Government House, and Britain suspends the constitution.

title: Enosis plebiscite
description: In a vote organised by the Church, almost all Greek Cypriots who sign ask for union with Greece.

title: EOKA campaign begins
description: Bombs across the island open the guerrilla war of EOKA against British rule and for union with Greece.

title: London and Zürich Agreements
description: Britain, Greece and Turkey agree on an independent Cyprus that may neither unite with Greece nor be partitioned.

title: Independence
description: The Republic of Cyprus comes into being with Archbishop Makarios as president and a Turkish Cypriot vice-president.

title: Bloody Christmas
description: Fighting between the two communities breaks out in Nicosia; Turkish Cypriots withdraw into enclaves and leave the government.

title: United Nations force arrives
description: The Security Council sets up a peacekeeping force for Cyprus, which is still there.

title: Coup against Makarios
description: The National Guard, led by officers from Greece, overthrows the president to bring about union with Greece; Turkey invades five days later.

title: Northern Cyprus declares independence
description: The Turkish Cypriot leadership proclaims the Turkish Republic of Northern Cyprus, which only Turkey recognises.

title: Crossings opened
description: The Turkish Cypriot authorities open the Ledra Palace crossing, and people cross the line for the first time in almost thirty years.

title: Annan Plan referendums
description: Turkish Cypriots accept the United Nations plan for reunification and Greek Cypriots reject it.

title: Cyprus joins the European Union
description: The whole island enters the European Union, but its law is suspended in the north.

title: Banking crisis
description: In return for an international loan, the second largest bank is closed and large depositors lose part of their money.
